issues.legal_issue: An admission that a person is not a member of a Scheduled Tribe is evidence against that person but does not conclusively determine tribal status or, by itself, estop the person from claiming that status.
material_facts: In a deed transferring land, the elected candidate stated that he did not claim to be a member of a Scheduled Tribe.
The deed was made shortly before the election, and the land-transfer restriction applicable to tribal members meant that the statement could help avoid refusal of registration.
The court considered the possibility that the candidate had consented to the statement in the deed.
issues.conclusion: The statement was evidence against the candidate but was not conclusive; the transferor was not disentitled from claiming Scheduled Tribe status and was not estopped from doing so on that ground alone.
issues.legal_principle: Whether a person belongs to a Scheduled Tribe specified under Article 342 of the Constitution is essentially a question of law. An express or implied admission to the contrary is evidence in an election petition but is not conclusive. A transfer made in breach of section 46 of the Chota Nagpur Tenancy Act, 1908, does not, by that fact alone, defeat the transferor’s claim to tribal status or create an estoppel.

predicates.election_petition: The dispute is an election petition in which a candidate’s eligibility based on tribal status is contested.
predicates.candidate_made_admission_against_tribal_: The candidate expressly or impliedly stated that they were not a member of the relevant tribal group.
predicates.admission_related_to_restricted_land_tra: The statement was made in connection with a land transfer subject to restrictions applicable to members of the tribal group.
predicates.admission_otherwise_offered_as_evidence: The statement was offered as evidence against the candidate’s claim of tribal status.

issues.definition: When an election petition relies on a candidate’s statement against their tribal status, including one connected with a restricted land transfer, the statement is evidence but does not conclusively resolve status or by itself prevent the candidate from claiming that status.

issues.legal_issue: Evidence may be used to determine whether an entry in a Presidential Scheduled Tribes Order encompasses a group asserted to be a sub-tribe of the named tribe, but it may not be used to add a distinct group to the Order.
material_facts: The candidate contended that Patars were Mundas, rather than a distinct community that should be treated as a Munda because of similarities with Mundas.

The parties presented oral and documentary evidence, including testimony about customs, social practices and intermarriage, historical and anthropological material, and records identifying Patars as Mundas.
The court considered earlier decisions concerning the use of evidence to interpret entries in constitutional lists.
issues.conclusion: Evidence was admissible to show whether the entry for Munda included Patars, but not to modify the Order by adding a distinct tribe or community.
issues.legal_principle: Article 342 of the Constitution authorizes the President to specify Scheduled Tribes and provides that the list may be altered by Parliament. Evidence may clarify what a listed entry was intended to mean, but courts may not use evidence to modify the list by including a distinct group. The court relied on B. Basavalingappa v. D. Munichinnappa, [1965] 1 S.C.R. 316; Bhaiyalal v. Harikishan Singh, [1965] 2 S.C.R. 877; Laxman Siddappa Naik v. Kattimani Chaniappa Jamappanna, [1968] 2 S.C.R. 805; and Dina v. Narayan Singh.

predicates.election_challenge_to_reserved_seat: The proceeding challenges a candidate’s eligibility to stand for a seat reserved for members of a tribal group.
predicates.claimant_relies_on_subtribe_identity: The candidate claims membership in a named tribe through a group said to be its sub-tribe, rather than claiming that a distinct group should itself be included.
predicates.evidence_is_offered_to_clarify_named_ent: Evidence is offered to establish what group an entry naming a tribe encompasses.

issues.definition: In a challenge to eligibility for a reserved seat, evidence offered to show that a claimant’s group falls within a named tribe may clarify the entry, but cannot add a distinct group to the list.

issues.legal_issue: A sub-tribe is not excluded from a general entry naming its tribe merely because the sub-tribe is not separately specified, and a candidate proved to belong to that sub-tribe falls within the entry.
material_facts: The Scheduled Tribes Order named Munda but did not separately name Patar.
The court found on the evidence that Patars were a sub-tribe of Mundas and were not different from Mundas.
The candidate stood for election from a constituency reserved for Scheduled Tribes.
issues.conclusion: The omission of Patar as a separate name did not exclude Patars from the general Munda entry; the candidate was a member of a Scheduled Tribe and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 342 of the Constitution and the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950, a group proved to be a sub-tribe of a tribe specified under a general entry is not excluded merely because it is not separately named. The inclusion of some sub-tribes does not, without more, imply the exclusion of others that fall within the general entry. Section 5 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 requires a candidate for a seat reserved for Scheduled Tribes to be a member of one of those tribes. The court relied on B. Basavalingappa v. D. Munichinnappa, [1965] 1 S.C.R. 316; Bhaiyalal v. Harikishan Singh, [1965] 2 S.C.R. 877; Laxman Siddappa Naik v. Kattimani Chaniappa Jamappanna, [1968] 2 S.C.R. 805; and Dina v. Narayan Singh.

rule.if: election_for_reserved_tribal_seat and general_entry_names_parent_tribe and subtribe_not_separately_named and evidence_shows_candidate_belongs_to_subtribe_of_named_tribe

predicates.election_for_reserved_tribal_seat: The candidate contests an election for a seat reserved for members of a tribal group.
predicates.general_entry_names_parent_tribe: The applicable list contains a general entry naming the tribe of which the candidate’s group is said to be a sub-tribe.
predicates.subtribe_not_separately_named: The candidate’s sub-tribe is not separately named in the applicable list.
predicates.evidence_shows_candidate_belongs_to_subt: The evidence establishes that the candidate belongs to a group that is a sub-tribe of the named tribe.

issues.definition: If a candidate in an election for a reserved tribal seat belongs to a sub-tribe of a named tribe, the sub-tribe’s omission as a separate name does not prevent the candidate from falling within the general entry.
